post.description:
Various endoints may return a 202 status response with
`callbackPayload` property in the body. Simply pass that
response to this endpoint to continue processing.

Endpoints with responses like this are structured as follows:
1. Call other endpoint.
2. Endpoint may return 202 with "callbackPayload" and progress.
3. Pass the callback payload to this endpoint.
4. This endpoint may return a 202 with another `callbackPayload`
5. Repeat until task is complete.

requestBody.description:
A secured JWT token containing:
- The original request userID.
- Instructions for the server on how to resume the original task.
- Context about the result of previous attempts.

The only way to get one of these payloads is to have it returned
from an /api/v2 endpoint as a `callbackPayload`.

This endpoint takes an access token created on your Hub and exchanges it for an access token that will work with the node. The access token makes a request back to the Hub to get the user's information and will SSO them into the node when the token is created.

By default, the access token lasts for 24 hours. You can control the expiry with the `dateExpires` parameter. Make sure you don't issue access tokens that last too long.

post.summary: Exchange an OAuth access token for a Vanilla access token.
post.description:
This endpoint takes an access token from your OAuth 2 provider and exchanges it for a Vanilla access token. If no matching user exists in Vanilla, one will be created and an access token will be issued for them.

In order to use this endpoint, the access token calls out to the API defined in the OAuth connection so it must have a scope that has access to the user's profile or else it will fail.

The access tokens provided by this endpoint are relatively short lived, so make sure you take note of the `dateExpires` in the response and have a strategy for refreshing the access token for long lived client sessions.

oauthAccessToken.description: Your OAuth access token with scope to access the user's profile information.

dateExpires.description: The date/time that the access token will expire.

403.description:
Forbidden. The OAuth access token didn't have permission to access the user information or failed in some other way.

If you get this error then make sure that the profile endpoint on **your** site returns a profile the access tokens you are providing to this site.

404.description: The provided client ID did not match the client ID that was configured within Vanilla.

500.description: OAuth is either not enabled or is not configured on Vanilla.

This is primarily intended for internal use on client-side code to authenticate to specific API endpoints where the response generated depends on the set of roles and associated permissions, but does not depend on the identity of the requesting user.

As many users may share a limited set of roles, this approach allows for caching responses to these endpoints for short periods, to improve overall page responsiveness while reducing server-side load.
